newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador rules out painful fiscal measures--for now.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador rules out painful fiscal measures--for now.

text.p: Caretaker President Fabian Alarcon Monday ruled out "for now" adopting major measures to lower Ecuador's $1.3 billion fiscal deficit.

"The won't be a major shock package," he told local radio. "The government is not planning, under current circumstances, to increase fuel prices or a new (electric) rate hike. I'm convinced the Ecuadorean people can't bear any new increase in taxes or rates," Alarcon added.
Last week, Alarcon ordered officials to draft a plan to fight the deficit by this week.
"We are making all efforts to avoid any measure that may entail an important social cost."
Alarcon wants to reduce the deficit to 2.3 percent of GDP by the end of the year from 6.6 percent of GDP, or $1.3 billion.
He has said he favors a tax reform to fight evasion that some estimates put at 60 percent.
Alarcon, who took over after President Abdala Bucaram was ousted by Parliament in February, must call elections in May 1998. The new president will take office on August 10, 1998.

Soon after taking power, Alarcon announced a plan to trim public spending that included electric and domestic fuel price hikes, although not as high as those Bucaram had announced before he was removed.
